notes: 2026-10-06: PSE&G HVAC and decarbonization tables read from the program's own page (myhomeenergy.pseg.com/heatingandcooling, tables are inside the page data). JCP&L Clean Comfort read from the official 2026 application PDF; JCP&L product pages read in full except the air source heat pump and ductless product pages, whose links are broken (only the 'up to' amounts on the category page are used). Atlantic City Electric read in a normal browser (homeenergysavings.atlanticcityelectric.com). NJ Clean Energy Program pages read in a normal browser. PSE&G GridSmart FAQ and WHES pages read directly. PSE&G EV charger page was read through a page summary tool, not word for word. Not read: Elizabethtown Gas, NJ Natural Gas and South Jersey Gas rebate tables; PSE&G thermostat marketplace terms beyond the instant-rebate list; the NJ sales tax exemption bulletin; community solar bill credits; Garden State Energy Storage residential amounts (proposal only). The state HOMES and HEAR federal rebates have no launch we could find (nj-29).

facts.program: PSE&G air source heat pump instant rebate
facts.claim: $300 for a split-system air source heat pump at Tier 1 (SEER2 15.2 or higher, EER2 11.7, HSPF2 7.8); $450 at Tier 2 (SEER2 17.1 or higher); single-package units $300 and $450 at lower EER2 and HSPF2 minimums; $600 for a cold climate air source heat pump (SEER2 15.2, EER2 10, HSPF2 8.1, COP 1.75 at 5 degrees F)
facts.eligibility: Current PSE&G residential customer with a valid account who owns the house where the work is done; participating contractor recommended (appliance rebates exist otherwise); no new construction or commercial property
facts.dates: No end date on the page; program is subject to change or termination without notice
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. The rebate appears as a line on the contractor's invoice. LMI customers get an extra $300 per eligible measure (nj-8). The page's meta text says up to $1,050 in instant savings, which is the gas combi boiler line, not a heat pump.

facts.claim: Gas or delivered fuel customers: lesser of $10,000 or 50% of the project cost of the largest system for a new cold climate air source heat pump that replaces the fossil heating system; low- to moderate-income customers: lesser of $12,000 or 60%. Also up to $2,000 for decommissioning, up to $2,000 for re-ducting, and $2,000 for every additional cold climate heat pump needed to meet the heat load
facts.eligibility: Current PSE&G residential electric customer (or Butler Electric customer on PSE&G gas) who owns a single-family or attached home of one to four units; no new construction or commercial property; NEEP-listed cold climate heat pump sized for at least 100% of the Manual J heat load, with Manual S and a decommissioning form
facts.dates: No end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 under 'Residential Building Decarbonization'. Ductless: SEER2 above 15, HSPF2 above 8.5, COP above 1.75 at 5 degrees F. Ducted: SEER2 above 14.3, HSPF2 above 7.7.

facts.program: PSE&G Clean Heat dual fuel and hybrid
facts.claim: Dual Heat (keep the old system, add a cold climate heat pump with integrated controls): lesser of $5,000 or 50% (income-qualified lesser of $6,000 or 60%), plus control unit rebates up to $1,500 per unit (two per dwelling). Hybrid Heat (heat pump covers cooling and up to 90% of heating): lesser of $2,000 or 30% (income-qualified lesser of $3,000 or 40%)
facts.amount: Up to $5,000 dual fuel; up to $2,000 hybrid
facts.eligibility: Gas or delivered fuel customers; integrated controls required; dual fuel heat pump sized for at least 100% of the Manual J heat load
facts.dates: No end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. Additional cold climate units: $2,000 each.

facts.claim: Gas customers: lesser of $3,000 per 10,000 BTUH or 50% of project cost; delivered fuel customers: lesser of $4,000 per 10,000 BTUH or 50%; low- to moderate-income customers get an extra $1,000 per 10,000 BTUH or 10% of project cost; plus up to $2,000 re-ducting and up to $2,000 decommissioning
facts.amount: Per 10,000 BTUH, up to 50% of cost
facts.eligibility: Open loop EER 21.1 and COP 4.1 or closed loop EER 17.1 and COP 3.6; loop design submitted; decommissioning form
facts.dates: No end date on the page

facts.claim: $750 for a heat pump water heater that replaces a fossil fuel storage or tankless water heater (gas or delivered fuel customers; UEF 2.2 or higher at 120V, 3.3 or higher at 240V); the standard HVAC instant rebate table lists $450; the appliance rebate page lists $750 as a post-purchase rebate
facts.eligibility: PSE&G residential customer; amount depends on the path (decarbonization $750 when replacing fossil fuel; HVAC table $450)
facts.dates: Appliance post-purchase applications within 120 days of purchase
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 on the HVAC page and https://myhomeenergy.pseg.com/rebates. The three listings do not say how they combine, so the page tells readers to ask the contractor which line applies.

facts.claim: Post-purchase: induction cooktop $250, electric dryer up to $300, washer up to $100, refrigerator up to $100, freezer up to $25, dishwasher $30, smart thermostat up to $100, heat pump water heater $750, tankless water heater $500, gas storage water heater $400. Instant discounts: room air conditioner $30, dehumidifier $40, air purifier $50, ceiling fan $35, ventilation fan $25
facts.eligibility: PSE&G customers; post-purchase applications up to 120 days after purchase
facts.dates: No end date on the page; subject to change or termination without notice
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. The program home page says up to $7,500 in qualifying rebates across categories; that total is not itemised.

facts.claim: Up to $100 post-purchase rebate on the appliance page; $60 instant rebate when installed as part of an HVAC install (ENERGY STAR certified, replacing a manual or programmable thermostat); PSE&G can also install an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat at no cost during a Whole Home Energy Assessment; the PSE&G Marketplace lists instant-rebate prices on ecobee and Google Nest models
facts.eligibility: PSE&G customer; marketplace devices installed within 60 days of purchase
facts.dates: No end date on the pages
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 (rebates page, HVAC page, Whole Home Energy Assessment page, marketplace.pseg.com).

facts.claim: Interest-free repayment on the monthly PSE&G bill: up to $25,000 for an HVAC Instant Rebates project; up to $50,000 for a standalone building decarbonization project (up to $2,000 of it for electrical upgrades unless income-qualified); up to $75,000 total for an HVAC project that includes decarbonization measures. Terms: 84 months; income-qualified customers 84 or 120 months on projects over $10,000
facts.eligibility: Qualified PSE&G residential customers (electric customers for the decarbonization allowance); 12 months of on-time payment history with PSE&G (a letter from a previous utility can substitute); no credit check; the account holder at the property signs
facts.dates: No end date on the page

facts.program: PSE&G low- to moderate-income HVAC bonus
facts.claim: An additional $300 per eligible measure in the HVAC Instant Rebates Program. Qualify by household income at or below 400% of the federal poverty level, or a primary residence in a low- or moderate-income census tract (self-certified), or participation in a listed safety-net program (such as SNAP, Lifeline, LIHEAP, NJ SHARES, Section 8, SSI, TANF, USF)
facts.eligibility: Income, census tract or safety-net participation
facts.dates: No end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. Income may need to be verified with documents.

facts.claim: Up to $5,000 in instant rebates on a home battery plus up to $25,000 in interest-free on-bill repayment. Approved batteries: Tesla Powerwall 3, Enphase 10C, and Enphase 5P (at least two). At least 8.5 kW of storage; new installations only; leases and existing batteries do not qualify; smart meter and Wi-Fi required; participants allow PSE&G to run the battery during up to 100 events a year of up to four hours each (not during outages)
facts.eligibility: Active PSE&G residential electric or dual-fuel account; participating contractor
facts.dates: No end date; the program is limited in total participants and is subject to change or termination
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 on the program FAQ and https://homeenergy.pseg.com/gridsmart. Rebate is a deduction on the contractor's invoice, not a bill credit. Solar panels are not covered but are allowed.

facts.claim: A free assessment of about one hour, a personal report, and no-cost products where limited supply allows: smart thermostat, LED bulbs, faucet aerators, efficient showerheads, water heater pipe insulation, advanced power strips, door sweeps, weather stripping and attic hatch insulation
facts.eligibility: PSE&G customers
facts.dates: No end date on the page

facts.claim: Free assessment and no-cost products, plus insulation upgrades in walls, ceilings and attic, weather stripping, duct sealing and HVAC tune-ups or replacements where needed. Qualify by at least one of: household income between 250% and 400% of the federal poverty level, a qualified moderate-income census tract (self-certified), NJ SHARES participation, or a home in a designated overburdened community
facts.eligibility: As listed
facts.dates: No end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 through a page summary tool; the products list matches the Whole Home Energy Assessment page. Below 250% of poverty, households use Comfort Partners (nj-22).

facts.claim: Customer-side make-ready up to $1,500 per charger; utility-side make-ready reduction of up to $5,000 on a required deposit; charger must be an ENERGY STAR certified Level 2 smart charger on a single residential meter, installed after January 27, 2021. The off-peak charging credit stopped taking new enrollments on January 13, 2026 and is discontinued on October 1, 2026
facts.amount: Up to $1,500 plus up to $5,000 toward utility work
facts.eligibility: PSE&G New Jersey electric customers in good standing
facts.dates: Approval can take up to three months
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 through a page summary tool, not word for word. Re-read in a normal browser at the monthly check.

facts.claim: Full displacement with a cold climate heat pump: gas or delivered fuel customers lesser of $10,000 or 50% of project cost; moderate-income lesser of $12,000 or 60%; up to $2,000 re-ducting; up to $2,000 decommissioning; $2,000 per additional cold climate heat pump and $750 per additional standard heat pump. Dual fuel: lesser of $5,000 or 50% (moderate-income $6,000 or 60%). Ground source: lesser of $4,000 per 10,000 Btu/h or 50% (gas) or $5,000 per 10,000 Btu/h (delivered fuel), plus $1,000 per 10,000 Btu/h or 10% for moderate-income. Heat pump water heater $750; induction cooking $400 ($600 moderate-income); heat pump clothes dryer $400; panel upgrade $300 per 240V circuit (up to four) or up to $4,000 for income-qualified
facts.eligibility: Existing single-family homes only (no new construction); existing heat must be gas, oil or propane; qualified contractor; permits; ENERGY STAR; AHRI and NEEP listing for cold climate
facts.dates: Purchased and installed February 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027; apply within 120 days of installation; allow 6 to 8 weeks
facts.notes: Read in full 2026-10-06 (application dated June 2026, 6 pages). Funds are subject to availability. 0% APR financing through neifund.org/jcpl-residential is named on the form.

facts.claim: Air source heat pumps (ENERGY STAR) up to $1,000; ductless mini-split heat pump up to $750; ductless mini-split cold climate up to $750; ground source heat pump up to $1,500; central air conditioners up to $200; ENERGY STAR smart thermostat $100 per unit; furnace fan $100; heat pump water heater $750. Tier tables were not readable
facts.amount: Up to $1,000 for an air source heat pump
facts.eligibility: New Jersey residential JCP&L customers; qualified electric equipment installed as a matched set
facts.dates: Purchased and installed January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027; apply within 120 days of purchase; subject to available funds
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. The air source and ductless product pages link to broken addresses, so only the 'up to' amounts from the category page are used. Terms read on the heat pump water heater product page.

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR electric clothes dryer up to $300; clothes washer up to $150; refrigerator up to $100; dehumidifier $40; room air conditioner $30; heat pump water heater $750
facts.eligibility: New Jersey residential JCP&L customers
facts.dates: January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027; apply within 120 days of purchase

facts.claim: Rebate of $2,000 plus $200 for each percentage point of modeled savings above 5%, capped at $7,500 and at 50% of cost; 0% loans for qualified applicants from $2,500 to $25,000 after the rebate (36, 60 or 84 months up to $10,000; 120 months from $10,001, and 120 months possible for income-qualified); air sealing must come before insulation
facts.eligibility: JCP&L residential account holder; participating contractor; at least 5% modeled savings
facts.dates: No end date on the page

facts.claim: No-cost upgrades of up to $14,000 and up to $2,500 in healthy home improvements, for households in a moderate-income census tract, in NJ SHARES, or with income above 250% and below 400% of the federal poverty level (one person: $39,901 to $63,840)
facts.eligibility: As listed; below 250% of poverty, use Comfort Partners
facts.dates: No end date on the page

facts.program: Atlantic City Electric HVAC Efficiency Program
facts.claim: Air source heat pump split or single-package: $500 at Tier 1 and $750 at Tier 2 (SEER2 17.1); ductless mini-split $750; cold climate heat pump $2,000 (limited time from April 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027); ENERGY STAR smart thermostat $150 (same limited time); heat pump water heater $750; furnace fan $100; central air conditioner $100 or $200; an extra $300 per qualified equipment for low- to moderate-income customers; headline up to $1,300
facts.eligibility: Atlantic City Electric residential customers; licensed HVAC contractor submits online
facts.dates: Limited-time cold climate and thermostat amounts April 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027; geothermal rebates effective for installs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 in a normal browser. The geothermal text on the page is hard to follow (new geothermal $10,000, ground-to-ground $2,500) so geothermal is only mentioned, not tabled.

facts.claim: Full displacement with a cold climate heat pump: up to $10,000 or 50% of project costs; partial displacement (dual fuel) cold climate: up to $5,000 or 50%; additional units $2,000 per cold climate or $750 per standard heat pump; partial displacement standard heat pump up to $2,000 or 30%; decommissioning 50% of itemized cost up to $2,000; electric ready panels up to $4,000 per house (income-qualified) or up to $300 per circuit; heat pump clothes dryer $200; induction stove $250 ($350 moderate-income)
facts.eligibility: Replacing gas, oil or propane equipment; contractor submits within 90 days of purchase
facts.dates: Application forms are numbered phases 1 and 2; no end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 in a normal browser (HVAC, panels and indoor appliance tabs).

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR clothes dryer up to $300; clothes washer up to $150; dehumidifier $40; refrigerator up to $100; room air conditioner $30; heat pump water heater $750; electric lawn equipment $25 to $75; electric riding mower $75; fossil fuel dryer to heat pump dryer up to $200; fossil fuel cooking to induction up to $250
facts.eligibility: Atlantic City Electric residential customers; checks mailed within 45 days
facts.dates: Program opened January 1, 2025 and ends December 31, 2026 or earlier if funding runs out
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. End date taken from the terms on the heat pump water heater product page (ace.clearesult.com/heat-pump-water-heater). The ACE electrification page says apply within 90 days.

facts.program: Atlantic City Electric Energy Wise Rewards
facts.claim: Enroll an eligible smart thermostat and get up to $100 for saving energy when demand is high
facts.eligibility: Atlantic City Electric customers with an eligible smart thermostat
facts.dates: No end date on the page
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. The enrollment page was not opened.

facts.claim: Free energy-saving measures for households at or below 250% of the federal poverty level (one person $39,900 a year, four people $82,500, eight people $139,300), or on TANF, Section 8, SNAP, SSI or General Assistance. Measures can include insulation, air sealing, duct sealing, a thermostat, efficient refrigerators and heating or cooling maintenance
facts.eligibility: Primary residence; ratepayer of record with a participating electric or gas utility; building of 14 or fewer individually metered units; oil, propane or kerosene heat goes to the state Office of Weatherization at 800-510-3102
facts.dates: Applications open on a rolling basis
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 in a normal browser. Phone 866-378-4345.

facts.claim: $1,500 at the dealership for a new eligible electric vehicle, plus $2,500 more (Charge Up+) for income-qualified buyers, $4,000 in all; up to $250 toward a qualifying Level 2 home charger
facts.eligibility: New Jersey residents; eligible vehicles and dealerships only; Charge Up+ must be pre-qualified before the sale or lease
facts.dates: Projected to remain available through June 2027; funds are limited
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 in a normal browser.

facts.claim: Net-metered residential solar earns SREC-II credits of $77 per megawatt-hour for registrations received on or after July 27, 2026 (it was $85 before). The residential block is 300 MW for Energy Year 2027; registration is first come, first served until the block is full or June 1, 2027, whichever is first
facts.eligibility: Net-metered residential projects registered through a solar contractor in the ADI portal
facts.dates: Registrations open until the block is full or June 1, 2027
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 in a normal browser. The length of the SREC-II term is not on this page and is not stated on our pages.

facts.claim: Customers get full retail credit for each kWh their system produces over the year. At the end of the 12-month period, leftover generation is credited at the wholesale value. Switching electric suppliers or changing the anniversary date credits the balance at the wholesale rate and starts a new cycle
facts.eligibility: Customer-generators with an interconnection agreement with their electric utility
facts.dates: Ongoing
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. A policy, not a cash rebate.

facts.program: New Jersey renewable energy property tax exemption
facts.claim: A residential property with a renewable energy system certified by the local enforcing agency may receive an exemption equal to the difference in assessed value before and after the system was installed. Apply with Form CRES to the tax assessor
facts.amount: Value added by the system is not taxed
facts.eligibility: Certified renewable energy system on the property
facts.dates: Ongoing
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06 through a page summary tool. Sales tax on solar was not confirmed from an official page and is not stated.

facts.claim: NJBPU released a straw proposal for Phase 2, Block 1 (about 150 MW) that outlines options to expand behind-the-meter residential battery storage. It is a proposal, with no residential incentive amounts or start date
facts.eligibility: Not defined
facts.dates: Straw proposal only
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. Goal of 2,000 MW of storage by 2030.

facts.program: Federal residential clean energy credits (25C, 25D) in New Jersey
facts.claim: Ended for spending after December 31, 2025
facts.eligibility: All homeowners
facts.dates: Ended December 31, 2025
facts.notes: Same IRS page used for the Pennsylvania facts. The NJBPU federal incentives page still lists these credits as running to 2032 and is out of date.

facts.program: New Jersey federal HOMES and HEAR home energy rebates
facts.claim: No launch date or customer amounts found on a state page. NJBPU's federal incentives page describes the HOMES and HEEHR design (for example 100% of cost for households under 80% of area median income) but does not say the rebates are open
facts.eligibility: Not defined
facts.dates: Unknown
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-06. A third-party site said the programs had not launched as of June 2026; that is not used as a source. Do not state these rebates as available.

facts.claim: Elizabethtown Gas, New Jersey Natural Gas and South Jersey Gas run their own rebate programs; the Atlantic City Electric HVAC application has joint forms with South Jersey Gas, New Jersey Natural Gas and PSE&G gas. Their amounts were not read
facts.eligibility: Gas customers of each utility
facts.dates: Unknown
facts.notes: Read only the joint-application list on 2026-10-06.
